crimes.name: Pilfer a Market Stall
crimes.ok: I slipped a pouch of dried herbs into my sleeve and walked on.
crimes.caught: A stall-keeper's apprentice caught my wrist mid-reach.

crimes.name: Cutpurse on Market Row
crimes.ok: A coin purse changed owners without its former owner noticing.
crimes.caught: The Low Watchpost bell rang before I cleared the bridge.

crimes.name: Break into a Cottage
crimes.ok: I left a cottage quieter than I found it, pockets heavier.
crimes.caught: A neighbor's dog and a lantern ended the night early.

crimes.name: Horse Theft
crimes.ok: A borrowed mount carried me farther than honesty would have.
crimes.caught: The brand on the saddle matched the Watch's ledger.

crimes.name: Resist the Watch
crimes.ok: I twisted free and lost myself in the crowd.
crimes.caught: The Watch put irons on me before the crowd finished gasping.

crimes.name: Tavern-Yard Brawl
crimes.ok: Fists settled what words could not. I walked away upright.
crimes.caught: The Watch broke it up and took names — mine first.

crimes.name: Smuggle Contraband
crimes.ok: Sealed crates crossed the quay without a customs stamp.
crimes.caught: A customs scribe found the false bottom.

crimes.name: Embezzle Guild Tithes
crimes.ok: Guild ledgers balanced because I made them balance.
crimes.caught: An auditor traced the missing grain to my name.

crimes.name: Waylay a Caravan
crimes.ok: The road paid better than honest work tonight.
crimes.caught: Caravan guards knew the trail better than I did.

crimes.name: Poison a Rival's Cup
crimes.ok: A quiet cup did louder work than any duel.
crimes.caught: The healer traced the bitter herb to my pouch.

crimes.name: Murder
crimes.ok: Someone who stood in my way no longer does.
crimes.caught: Blood and witnesses told the same story.

crimes.name: Bribe a Court Clerk
crimes.ok: A sealed letter moved faster after coin changed hands.
crimes.caught: The clerk kept the coin and the complaint.

crimes.name: Forge a Seal
crimes.ok: Wax and patience bought me a name that was not mine.
crimes.caught: The true seal-keeper knew their own ridges.

crimes.name: Extort a Merchant
crimes.ok: Fear paid on time. The merchant smiled with empty eyes.
crimes.caught: The merchant smiled for the Watch instead.

crimes.name: Desecrate a Shrine
crimes.ok: Offerings left for gods found a new altar — my purse.
crimes.caught: A priest's apprentice raised the alarm.

crimes.name: Sell Court Favors
crimes.ok: Ink and influence cost what the highest bidder paid.
crimes.caught: A rival posted the ledger where the plaza could read it.
